editorial:
Imagine falling head-over-heels for someone, only for them to actually die for a few minutes and then just wake back up. That is exactly what happens to Elisabeth and Simon. They are in that honeymoon phase of a new relationship when this scary medical fluke hits. Instead of just being happy he is okay, the whole mood shifts. You get to see them struggle with the fear that it could happen again and how it changes the way they look at their future together. It feels like a deep conversation between friends where everyone is trying to figure out the meaning of life while avoiding the scary parts.

What really works here is how the movie focuses on the talking. Once they tell their friends, the Martignacs, things get spicy because of their different views on religion and death. The acting is very natural, though the pacing is slow, so you will need some patience. If you enjoy stories that make you think about love and loss, you should definitely check this out. It looks great if you can find the 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection, but renting it on Apple TV is a quick way to see if you like the style.
endingExplained: As the movie wraps up, the focus shifts from the medical scare to the emotional toll it took on everyone. You see the characters realize that death is the only thing that makes love feel urgent and real. There is no big shocking twist, but rather a quiet acceptance. Simon and Elisabeth decide to keep living their lives despite the risk, accepting that their time is limited and precious.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slow stories about love and philosophy.
